name: Boeing 737-900
sources: [NG] Boeing D6-58325-7 Rev C (October 2025), Next-Generation 737 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/737NG_REV_C.pdf. 737-900 and 737-900ER (fig 2.2.7, p.2-15): overall length 42.11 m (138 ft 2 in), fuselage 40.67 m, span 34.32 m, engine inlet 14.9 m (49 ft 0 in) and wingtip 26.57 m (87 ft 2 in) aft of the nose, nose gear 4.09 m aft of the nose, wheelbase 17.17 m (56 ft 4 in), track 5.72 m. 737-800 (fig 2.2.5, p.2-13): overall length 39.47 m (129 ft 6 in), fuselage 38.02 m, span 34.32 m, inlet 13.36 m (43 ft 10 in), wingtip 24.99 m (82 ft 0 in), nose gear 4.09 m, wheelbase 15.60 m (51 ft 2 in), track 5.72 m.

Fuselage [NG]: the 737-900 is 2.64 m (8 ft 8 in) longer than the 737-800. The inlet, the wingtip and the main gear are on the wing, and each is 5 ft 2 in (1.57 m) further from the nose (with winglets too: the winglet's tip 85 ft 4 in against 90 ft 6 in, fig 2.2.6 and 2.2.8; the wheelbase also in fig 7.2.1, p.7-5), while the nose gear stays 4.09 m from it: 1.57 m more ahead of the wing. The rest, 3 ft 6 in (1.07 m), is behind the wing. 1.57 + 1.07 = 2.64 m = 42.11 - 39.47 m: no rest.

The words of [NG] do not agree with its dimensions. Section 1.3 (p.1-3) says that the 737-900 is 96 in longer than the 737-800, with a 54-in section ahead of the wing and a 42-in section behind it: 8 in less than its own two lengths. Fig 2.2.8 (p.2-16) puts the inlet of the 737-900 with winglets at 48 ft 4 in, 54 in more than the 737-800's, where fig 2.2.7 has 49 ft 0 in. The recipe follows the dimensions (62 in ahead, 42 in behind). [MAX] Boeing D6-38A004 Rev H (March 2023) https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/737MAX_RevH.pdf gives the same for the same two fuselages, 737-8 against 737-9: wheelbase 15.60 m against 17.17 m, inlet 42 ft 8 in against 47 ft 10 in (fig 2.2.2 and 2.2.3, p.2-10, 2-11); the overwing exits 54 ft 10 in and 58 ft 0 in against 60 ft 0 in and 63 ft 2 in from the nose, each 62 in more; the aft cargo door and the aft entry door each 104 in more (fig 2.7.1, p.2-26).

Doors: entry door no. 1 is 5.03 m (16 ft 6 in) from the nose on all models ([NG] fig 2.7.1, p.2-33). The aft entry door is 34.52 m (113 ft 3 in) from the nose: the 737-800's 31.88 m (104 ft 7 in, [NG] fig 2.7.5, p.2-37) and 2.64 m; [MAX] fig 2.7.1 prints 113 ft 3 in (34.52 m) for the 737-9. [NG] fig 2.7.5 prints 108 ft 1 in (32.92 m) for the 737-900: that is the 737-800's door moved by the aft 42 in only, and it is not where [NG] draws the door. Measured on the cabin plans of [NG] (the scale from the 32-in seat pitch, the origin from door 1 at 5.03 m): aft door 34.52 m, overwing exits 18.28 m and 19.24 m on the 737-900 (fig 2.4.7, p.2-27); aft door 34.51 m, overwing exits 18.27 m and 19.23 m on the 737-900ER (fig 2.4.8, p.2-28). [MAX] has the 737-9's overwing exits at 18.29 m and 19.25 m.

Mid exit door: the 737-900ER has a second pair of doors behind the wing ([NG] section 1.3, p.1-4: "Additional exit doors are installed aft of the wing"; table 2.1.5, p.2-6, names it the mid exit door). Fig 2.4.8 (p.2-28) marks it in both walls with a centre line, as it marks door 1 and the aft door, with an attendant's seat beside it: 26.69 m from the nose, measured as above. [MAX] fig 2.7.1 lists the 737-9's mid exit door with the passenger doors, 87 ft 7 in (26.70 m) from the nose. The base does not have this door, thus the recipe has stations of its own: door 1, the mid exit door, the aft door. The 737-900 that is not an ER does not have it (fig 2.4.7, p.2-27): for that aircraft, remove 26.7 from the doors. Cockpit windows: the base's 2.92 m (the same nose).

Wingtip [NG]: the base's mesh has the blended winglets (737-800W). 737-800W (fig 2.2.6, p.2-14) and 737-900W, 737-900ERW (fig 2.2.8, p.2-16): span 35.79 m (117 ft 5 in) on both; at OEW the winglet's bottom is 4.32 m and its tip 6.76 m above the ground on both (table 2.3.3, p.2-19). The same wing and the same winglet: no change.

Nacelles [NG]: the CFM56-7 on every model (section 1.3, p.1-4), its axis 4.83 m from the centre line on both (fig 2.2.5, 2.2.7); engine ground clearance 0.64 m at OEW and 0.48 m at the maximum taxi weight on both (table 2.3.2, p.2-18). No change.

Gear [NG] fig 7.2.1, p.7-5: two wheels on each leg, track 5.72 m, nose tyres 27x7.75-15 and main tyres H44.5x16.5-21 on the 737-800, the 737-900 and the 737-900ER. Only the wheelbase differs: 17.17 m = 15.60 + 1.57 m. The base's gear is kept.
